bundled documentation. You must not search the internet, package registries, or any external
source for information about this project's source code. Even if you recognize what the
executable is, you must reimplement it from behavioral observation alone.

- Downloading the project from package registries: `cargo install <project>`, `go get github.com/<org>/<project>`, `pip install <project>`, `apt-get source <project>`, `npm install <project>`, etc.

# jplot

Jplot tracks expvar-like (JSON) metrics and plot their evolution over time right into your iTerm2, Kitty terminal, or terminals with DRCS Sixel Graphics support.

![](doc/demo.gif)

Above capture is jplot monitoring a Go service's expvar:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars \
    memstats.HeapSys+memstats.HeapAlloc+memstats.HeapIdle+marker,counter:memstats.NumGC \
    counter:memstats.TotalAlloc \
    memstats.HeapObjects \
    memstats.StackSys+memstats.StackInuse
```

By default, jplot uses the full size of the terminal, but it is possible to limit the render to a few rows:

![](doc/rows.gif)

## Install

Using homebrew:

```
brew install rs/tap/jplot
```

This tool works with [iTerm2](https://www.iterm2.com), [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/), [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/), or terminals that support DRCS Sixel Graphics.

## Usage

Given the following JSON output:

```
{
    "mem": {
        "Heap": 1234,
        "Sys": 4321,
        "Stack": 203
    },
    "cpu": {
        "STime": 123,
        "UTime":1234
    },
    "Threads": 2
}
```

You can graph the number of thread over time:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars Threads
```

![](doc/single.png)

Or create a graph with both Utime and Stime growth rate on the same axis by using `+` between two field paths:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars counter:cpu.STime+counter:cpu.UTime
```

Note: the `counter:` prefix instructs jplot to compute the difference between the values instead of showing their absolute value.

![](doc/dual.png)


Or create several graphs by providing groups of fields as separate arguments; each argument creates a new graph:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars mem.Heap+mem.Sys+mem.Stack counter:cpu.STime+cpu.UTime Threads
```

![](doc/all.png)

### Spec Syntax

Each positional arguments given to jplot create a stacked graph with the specified values. To reference the values, use JSON query syntax. Several value paths can be referenced for the same graph by using the `+` character to separate them.

In addition, each value path can be prefixed with options separated from the path by a column. Several options can be used for the same command by separating them with a comma like so: `option1,option2:value.path`.

Supported options are:
* `counter`: Computes the difference with the last value. The value must increase monotonically.
* `marker`: When the value is none-zero, a vertical line is drawn.

## Recipes

### Memstats

Here is an example command to graph a Go program memstats:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars \
    memstats.HeapSys+memstats.HeapAlloc+memstats.HeapIdle+marker,counter:memstats.NumGC \
    counter:memstats.TotalAlloc \
    memstats.HeapObjects \
    memstats.StackSys+memstats.StackInuse
```

![](doc/memstats.png)

### Vegeta

With the help of jaggr, jplot can be used to integrate vegeta as follow:

```
echo 'GET http://localhost:8080' | \
    vegeta attack -rate 5000 -workers 100 -duration 10m | vegeta dump | \
    jaggr @count=rps \
          hist\[100,200,300,400,500\]:code \
          p25,p50,p95:latency \
          sum:bytes_in \
          sum:bytes_out | \
    jplot rps+code.hist.100+code.hist.200+code.hist.300+code.hist.400+code.hist.500 \
          latency.p95+latency.p50+latency.p25 \
          bytes_in.sum+bytes_out.sum
```

![](doc/vegeta.gif)

### Supported Terminals

* [xterm](http://invisible-island.net/xterm/)
* [iTerm2](https://www.iterm2.com/) on OSX
* [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/) on Linux/macOS/Windows
* [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/) on Linux/macOS/Windows
* [mintty](https://mintty.github.io/) on UNIX OSs via SSH
* [mlterm](https://sourceforge.net/projects/mlterm/) on Linux and Windows
* [RLogin](http://nanno.dip.jp/softlib/man/rlogin/) on Windows
* [yaft](http://uobikiemukot.github.io/yaft/) on Linux console
* [yaft-android](https://github.com/uobikiemukot/yaft-android) on Android
* [Tanasinn](http://saitoha.github.io/tanasinn/) on Firefox/Thunderbird

# 2. else check FIELD_SPEC -> if missing, print Usage
# 3. else check window size -> ...
# So to get past graphics check we need either TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app OR logic includes other terms? Let's explore detection.
# The earlier brute force showed plain TERM=xterm* fails, but TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app passes (shows Usage). So graphics detection is based on TERM_PROGRAM env var equals "iTerm.app" ?

# What about other terminals that support sixel/kitty? Maybe checks $TERM contains "xterm" plus some fallback? But our env with TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app inside tmux still shows usage, so that bypasses.

# But also we saw that running without TERM_PROGRAM but inside tmux still fails. So need to find all conditions that make it pass.
# Let's more systematically test:

# Check what jplot checks: might check for iTerm2 via TERM_PROGRAM, for Kitty via KITTY_WINDOW_ID or term.contains("kitty"), for sixel via TERM containing "xterm"? But our earlier test with TERM=xterm-256color failed, so not just that.

# Let's test more combinations: maybe it checks stdout is tty + TERM env? But we saw when TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app and not in tty, it still passed graphics check (got to usage), then later failed on window size check. So graphics check does NOT require tty, only env var? Wait earlier we had no field spec and it passed to usage even when piped. So graphics check is env-only, not tty-dependent.

# Let's test which envs make it pass graphics check and go to next stage (either usage or window size error).

test_graphics() {
  local envs="$1"
  local cmd="$2"
  output=$(env $envs $cmd 2>&1 | head -n 1)
  echo "$envs -> $output" | od -c | head -n 1
  # more readable
  echo "$envs -> $(env $envs $cmd 2>&1 | head -n 1 | cat -A)"
}

for envval in "TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app" "KITTY_WINDOW_ID=1" "TERM=xterm-256color" "TERM=screen" "TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app TERM=xterm-256color" "COLORTERM=truecolor" "TERM=kitty" "TERM_PROGRAM=kitty" "TERM_PROGRAM=WezTerm"; do
  printf "env %s: " "$envval"
  env $envval ./executable 2>&1 | head -n 1 | od -An -tx1 | head
  env $envval ./executable 2>&1 | head -n 1 | cat -A
done

# try also checking for Sixel: maybe checks TERM contains "mlterm" or "yaft" etc mentioned in docs?

for t in xterm xterm-256color xterm-kitty mlterm yaft kitty; do
  echo -n "TERM=$t: "
  env TERM=$t ./executable 2>&1 | head -n 1 | cat -A
done

# Check if checking for existence of env vars rather than value
for var in ITERM_SESSION_ID KITTY_WINDOW_ID TERM_PROGRAM COLORTERM; do
  echo -n "$var dummy: "
  env $var=dummy ./executable 2>&1 | head -n 1 | cat -A
done

echo "===with field spec and piped ==="
for envval in "TERM_PROGRAM=iTerm.app" "KITTY_WINDOW_ID=1" "TERM=xterm-256color"; do
  printf 'env %s + stdin json: ' "$envval"
  printf '{"a":1}\n' | env $envval ./executable "a" 2>&1 | head -n 1 | cat -A
done
"}

import subprocess, pty, os, time, fcntl, termios, struct, select

def run(env, inputs, steps=4):
    master, slave = pty.openpty()
    winsize = struct.pack("HHHH", 24, 80, 0, 0)
    fcntl.ioctl(slave, termios.TIOCSWINSZ, winsize)
    cmd = f"env {env} ./executable -steps {steps} 'a' 'b'"
    proc = subprocess.Popen(cmd, shell=True, stdin=subprocess.PIPE, stdout=slave, stderr=slave)
    for line in inputs:
        proc.stdin.write((line+"\n").encode())
    proc.stdin.close()
    time.sleep(0.3)
    os.set_blocking(master, False)
    data=b''
    iteration=0
    while iteration <15:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.8)
        if not r:
            print(f"no data iter {iteration} poll {proc.poll()}")
            iteration+=1
            if iteration>5:
                break
            continue
        chunk=os.read(master,8192)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data+=chunk
        print(f"iter {iteration} chunk {repr(chunk[:700])} len {len(chunk)}")
        if b"ReportCellSize" in chunk and b"File" not in chunk:
            print("iterm probe -> resp")
            os.write(master, b"\x1b]1337;ReportCellSize=20;10\x07")
        elif b"_Gi=1,a=q" in chunk:
            print("kitty query -> err to fallback")
            os.write(master, b"\x1b_Gi=1;ENOTSUP\x1b\\")
        elif b"\x1b[c" in chunk:
            print("DA query -> resp 62")
            os.write(master, b"\x1b[?62c")
        elif b"\x1b[14t" in chunk:
            print("14t query -> resp")
            os.write(master, b"\x1b[4;480;800t")
        elif b"ReportCellSize" in chunk and b"File" in chunk:
            print("IMAGE iterm")
        elif b"_Ga=T" in chunk:
            print("IMAGE kitty")
        elif b"\x1bP" in chunk:
            print("IMAGE sixel")
        # handle embedded queries inside same chunk
        if b"\x1b[c" in chunk and b"_Gi=" in chunk:
            print("both")
        iteration+=1
        if b"1337;File" in data or b"_Ga=T" in data or b"\x1bP" in data:
            # we got image, but continue to drain?
            for _ in range(5):
                r2,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.5)
                if not r2:
                    break
                chunk2=os.read(master, 8192)
                if not chunk2:
                    break
                data+=chunk2
                print(f"image chunk len {len(chunk2)} {repr(chunk2[:200])}")

    time.sleep(0.5)
    while True:
        r,_,_=select.select([master],[],[],0.3)
        if not r:
            break
        chunk=os.read(master,8192)
        if not chunk:
            break
        data+=chunk
        print(f"drain {repr(chunk[:600])} len {len(chunk)}")
        if b"ReportCellSize" in chunk and b"File" not in chunk:
            os.write(master, b"\x1b]1337;ReportCellSize=20;10\x07")
        elif b"_Gi=1,a=q" in chunk:
            os.write(master, b"\x1b_Gi=1;ENOTSUP\x1b\\")
        elif b"\x1b[c" in chunk:
            os.write(master, b"\x1b[?62c")
        elif b"\x1b[14t" in chunk:
            os.write(master, b"\x1b[4;480;800t")

    has_file = b"1337;File" in data
    has_kitty = b"_Ga=T" in data
    has_sixel = b"\x1bP" in data
    print(f"final poll {proc.poll()} total {len(data)} has_file {has_file} has_kitty {has_kitty} has_sixel {has_sixel}")
    #print(data[-800:])
    proc.terminate()
    try: proc.wait(timeout=1)
    except: proc.kill()
    os.close(master); os.close(slave)
    return data

print("=== iterm ===")

# jplot

Jplot tracks expvar-like (JSON) metrics and plot their evolution over time right into your iTerm2, Kitty terminal, or terminals with DRCS Sixel Graphics support.

![](doc/demo.gif)

Above capture is jplot monitoring a Go service's expvar:

```
jplot --url http://:8080/debug/vars \
    memstats.HeapSys+memstats.HeapAlloc+memstats.HeapIdle+marker,counter:memstats.NumGC \
    counter:memstats.TotalAlloc \
    memstats.HeapObjects \
    memstats.StackSys+memstats.StackInuse
```

By default, jplot uses the full size of the terminal, but it is possible to limit the render to a few rows:

![](doc/rows.gif)

## Install

Using homebrew:

```
brew install rs/tap/jplot
```

This tool works with [iTerm2](https://www.iterm2.com), [Kitty](https://sw.kovidgoyal.net/kitty/), [Warp](https://www.warp.dev/), or terminals that support DRCS Sixel Graphics.
